orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
 AT NAINITAL
THE HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SRI VIPIN SANGHI 
AND 
THE HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI 
WRIT PETITION (PIL) NO. 15 OF 2022
23RD FEBRUARY, 2023
Between: 
Matri Sadan Jagjeetpur, Kankhal …… Petitioner 
 
and 
Union of India and others …… Respondents 
 Counsel for the petitioner : Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, learned counsel 
 Counsel for respondent No. 1 : Mr. Karan Anand, learned Standing Counsel 
for the Union of India 
 Counsel for respondent Nos. 2, 6 to 9 : Mr. A.S. Rawat, learned Senior Counsel 
(Special Counsel) with Mr. C.S. Rawat, 
learned Chief Standing Counsel for the 
State 
 Counsel for respondent No. 3 : Mr. Rajeev Bhatt, learned counsel 
 Counsel for respondent No. 4 : Mr. Aditya Pratap Singh, learned counsel 
 Counsel for respondent No. 5 : Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned counsel 
 Counsel for respondent No. 10 : Mr. Saurav Adhikari, learned counsel 
 Counsel for the intervener : Mr. U.K. Uniyal, learned Senior Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Piyush Garg and Mr. Nikhil 
Singhal, learned counsels 
 
The Court made the following: 
ORDER: (per Hon’ble The Chief Justice Sri Vipin Sanghi) 
 An affidavit has been filed by the 
respondent No. 10-NMCG in pursuance of our order dated   2
15.12.2022. Along with the said affidavit, communication 
issued by the Secretary, Department of Water Resources, 
River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation dated 
31.01.2022, addressed to the Secretary, Ministry of 
Environment, Forests and Climate Change, has been 
enclosed, which requests that the issue of sand mining on 
river Ganga in Kumbh zone be reviewed keeping into 
consideration holistic status of mining in the said 
stretches, i.e., the stretch between Raiwala to Bhogpur, 
keeping in view its impact on river morphology and 
ecology. 
2. It appears that no further review has taken 
place at the end of the Ministry of Environment, Forests 
and Climate Change. At least, no further decision of the 
said Ministry has been placed before us. 
3. We direct the Ministry of Environment, Forests 
and Climate Change to place before us their stand in the 
light of the letter dated 31.01.2022 aforesaid. 
4. The response should be filed within the next ten 
days keeping in view the urgency in the matter. 
5. Copy of the affidavit filed by the NMCG shall be 
provided to the counsel for respondent No. 1 during the   3
course of the day by the learned counsel for the 
petitioner, along with its annexures. 
6. List on 17.03.2023, along with connected 
matter. 
7. Interim orders to continue till the next date of 
listing. 
8. This order be also communicated to the Ministry 
of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, Government 
of India, by the Registrar General of this Court, within 24 
hours for compliance. 
 
 _________________
 VIPIN SANGHI, C.J. 
 ___________________ 
MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J. 
Dt: 23rd FEBRUARY, 2023 
Negi

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Brahmachari Dayanand, petitioner in 
person in WPPIL Nos. 15 of 2022 and 66 of 
2022.
Mr. Prabhakar Joshi, Advocate for the 
petitioners in WPPIL No. 16 of 2016.
Mr. R.S. Bisht, Addl. CSC for the 
State.
Mr. I.D. Paliwal, Standing Counsel for 
the State of U.P.
Mr. Saurav Adhikar, Standing 
Counsel for the Union of India.
Mr. Rajeev Bhatt, Advocate for the 
Central Pollution Control Board.
Mr. Aditya Pratap Singh, Advocate for 
the Uttarakhand Environment Protection 
and Pollution Control Board.
Mr. V.K. Kapurwan, Advocate for the 
Uttarakhand Forest Development 
Corporation.
Arguments heard, but not concluded.
A report is submitted by the District 
Magistrate, Haridwar pursuant to order 
dated 26.07.2024 of this Court, but it has 
been heavily disputed by the petitioners.
On 16.03.2022, this Court had passed 
an order that no mining activity shall take 
place in the area in question.  The Court has once issued a 
Commission also, the report of which 
reveals that stone crushers are working in 
defiance to the Court’s order and mining 
activities are being done by automatic 
machines. 
Now, it appears that the reports, 
which are being submitted by the State 
Authorities are hiding more than revealing. 
The Court requested the learned counsel for 
the Central Pollution Control Board and he
agreed that the representative of the 
Central Pollution Control Board would visit 
the area and submit a report with regard to 
mining activities that are being undertaken 
in the area in question, particularly the 
mechanized or automatic machines are 
being used or not, and also the location of 
the stone crushers and their working. 
The representatives of Central 
Pollution Control Board may be assisted by 
the petitioner, the representative of the 
Regional Office of the Uttarakhand State 
Pollution Control Board as well as by the 
District Magistrate, Haridwar.
The report by the Central Pollution 
Control be filed on or before the next date of 
listing i.e. 21.02.2025.
This Court is of the opinion that 
somewhere an officer of the administration 
should be held accountable.
Today, the petitioner in WPPIL No. 15 
of 2022 has placed for perusal of the Court 
some coloured photographs showing 
indiscriminate mining by mechanized or 
automatic machines, trucks. 
On 16.03.2022, this Court had 
stopped mining in the area in question. The 
Court directs the Senior Superintendent of 
Police, Haridwar to ensure the compliance 
of the Court’s order. Any defiance shall be 
considered as a disobedience by the Senior  Superintendent of Police, Haridwar. He may 
use such force as is necessary to ensure 
compliance of the Court’s order. 
List this matter on 21.02.2025 at 
02:00 p.m.
On that date, the District Magistrate, 
Haridwar and the Senior Superintendent of 
Police, Haridwar are requested to join the 
proceedings through video conferencing. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
14.02.2025

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPPIL No. 15 of 2022
With
WPPIL No. 66 of 2022
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Brahmchari Sudhanand Aka 
Saurabh, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, C.S.C. with Mr. 
Gajendra Tripathi, Brief Holder for the 
State.
Mr. Saurav Adhikari, Standing 
Counsel for the Union of India.
Mr. Rajeev Bhatt, Advocate for the 
Central Pollution Control Board.
Mr. Aditya Pratap Singh, Advocate for 
the Uttarakhand Environment Protection 
and Pollution Control Board.
Mr. V.K. Kapruwan, Advocate for the 
Uttarakhand Forest Development 
Corporation.
Heard.
On 14.02.2025, this Court has 
requested the Central Pollution Control 
Board (“CPCB”)to visit the area and submit 
a report with regard to the mining activities 
that are being undertaken in the area in 
question particularly as to whether, 
mechanized or automatic machines are 
used or not.
The report has already been 
submitted by the CPCB. 
Today, during the course of hearing 
Mr. Arvind Kumar, Scientist C and Mr. 
Vinay K. Upadhyay, Scientist C, CPCB, 
also joined the proceedings through video 
conferencing.
The petitioner has also filed response 
to the report submitted by CPCB. 
The report of CPCB reveals as if the  mining activity is already going on in the 
area in question. There were tyre marks in 
the mining areas. The minerals were found 
deposited in some of the stone crushers 
which were visited by the CPCB team. 
These stone crushers had no CTO.
How it is being done? In fact, on 
14.02.2025, this Court had requested the 
District Magistrate, Haridwar and Senior 
Superintendent of Police, Haridwar to join 
the proceedings through video 
conferencing. They are not present today.
Learned C.S.C. would submit that 
they were to join, but it appears that there 
was some disruption in the video 
conferencing.
Let both of them join the proceedings 
through video conferencing tomorrow at 
2:00 P.M.
During the course of hearing, the
learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that, in fact, the stone crushers were 
closed within the radius of 5 Km from the 
river bed. He would submit that pursuant 
to one such order passed in WPPIL No. 62 
of 2016, 48 stone crushers had already 
been closed, but they were de-sealed 
without any further order of this Court. He 
would also submit that, in fact, National 
Green Tribunal has also passed directions 
for shifting the stone crushers from within 
5 Km limit of river bed. He also refers to 
various orders of CPCB and NMCG. 
Referring a letter dated 16.02.2015 of the 
District Magistrate, Dehradun, he argued 
that, in fact, all the stone crushers within 
5 Km radius of river bed should be closed
so as to prevent illegal mining.
This Court had already passed order 
for banning mining in the area in question. 
But, it appears that orders of this Court 
are not being enforced. This is a serious 
issue.
The Court requested learned counsel 
for the Union of India as to whether the  127 Infantry Battalion (TA) Eco, Garhwal 
Rifles may assist this Court in the matter.
He submits that he will contact the officers 
and will revert tomorrow. 
Let a Senior Officer, who have 
experience in the relevant field, from 127 
Infantry Battalion (TA) Eco, Garhwal Rifles 
may join the proceedings tomorrow at 2:00 
P.M. to assist the Court in the matter. 
The Court posed a question to learned 
C.S.C. as to why the stone crushers may 
not be shifted beyond 5 Km radius of the 
river bed?
In fact, during the course of hearing, 
learned counsel for the Uttarakhand 
Environment Protection and Pollution 
Control Board would submit that in WPMB 
No. 281 of 2025, this Court has already 
passed direction directing the Secretary, 
Mining, Government of Uttarakhand and 
the Uttarakhand Pollution Control Board 
to identify areas in every district, which 
can be earmarked as dedicated zones for 
crushing and dumping of stones/RBM. 
Cannot it be done in District Haridwar by 
locating all 121 stone crushers beyond the 
radius of 5 Kms from the river bed. 
Automatic/electronic monitoring of the 
vehicles and entry of ravannas on the 
portal may also be some of the steps to 
ensure that mining is not being done in the 
area, in which this Court has banned it.
Learned C.S.C. submits that he would 
get instruction and revert back to this 
Court.
List on 12.06.2025 at 2:00 PM.
Also place record of WPPIL No. 62 of 
2016 at the time of hearing
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 11.06.2025
Jitendra
